title: Runs: a run keeps the chat it was started beside (POST /hub/runs {chat?}, GET /hub/runs?chat=<id>)
operator_decision: 2026-10-08 (TRACK.md, USER GRAPH DESIGN): the inspector's graph tab shows the inspected chat's runs as sub-tabs, and with no chat open every perch run. A perch run must therefore record the chat the page had open when it was started; today a run has no chat link (state.rs:112-148 has no such field).
why: The page can only scope the strip to a chat if the perch keeps the chat on the run and can list one chat's runs. Filtering only in the page is not enough: the list is the newest LISTED = 50 of every chat (state.rs:54, 480) while runs.json keeps KEPT = 500 (state.rs:53), so a chat's older runs would drop out of its strip once 50 newer runs exist anywhere.
what:
All in perch/src/runs/state.rs. The chat is a LABEL: it is checked with sessions::id_ok (sessions.rs:66-73: first character an ASCII letter or digit, then [A-Za-z0-9._-], 128 bytes at most), so it is one safe path component, but it is never joined to a path anyway.

POST /hub/runs {graph, args?, chat?} (create, state.rs:498-557):
- chat absent or JSON null: no tag. The answer and runs.json are byte-for-byte what they are today.
- chat a string that passes id_ok: the tag. Anything else (a number, a bool, an object, "", "../x", "a/b", "a\nb", "%2e", ".x", 129 bytes) is a 400 via problem() with the sentence `chat is a chat's id: a letter or digit, then letters, digits, '.', '_' or '-', 128 bytes at most`.
- The shape check goes right after the args cap (state.rs:511-514) and before the graph check (state.rs:516), so a refused chat makes nothing: tests/runs.rs:396 holds that rule for every refusal.
- Existence: after the --home check (state.rs:526-528) and before the cheap holder check (state.rs:530) and the health gate (state.rs:533), so an unknown chat never costs the 1 s service probes.
  - The rule is the one the operator's terminal already uses (term/routes.rs:145-156): the chat is known if `registry.known_cwd(id)` (sessions.rs:531-534) is Some, or `registry.list().iter().any(|row| row.id == id)` (sessions.rs:796-798).
  - It runs under tokio::task::spawn_blocking, as term does (term/routes.rs:104-107), because list() reads directories.
  - Write it as a private `fn chat_known(registry: &sessions::Registry, id: &str) -> bool` in state.rs with a comment naming its twin in term/routes.rs. Do not edit sessions.rs or term/ (one shared Registry::knows is a follow-up for their owners).
  - Unknown: refuse(StatusCode::NOT_FOUND, "no such chat", Value::Null), term's words (term/routes.rs:108). It is a body with a sentence, so the page tells it from the empty 404 of an unknown graph. A join error: 500 "the chat could not be read" (term/routes.rs:111).
- Storage: `Run.chat: Option<String>` after `args`, `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]`, like every optional field (state.rs:117-147). A runs.json written by today's perch still loads.
  - `Run::new(graph, args, chat)` (state.rs:151) and `Store::begin(home, graph, args, chat)` (state.rs:297) put the tag in the SAME write as the new row (state.rs:324-331).
  - Never set it through edit() afterwards: that would be a second write and a window where the run exists without its tag.
  - edit, resume, give_back, Verdict::apply and adopt clone or keep the whole record, so the tag survives them unchanged; check that, change none of them.
- The chat never reaches eidolon. It is not in start_argv, the run's config.toml, args.json, the child's environment, any path or file name, or a tracing line. proc.rs is not touched. The doc paragraph at state.rs:35-37 (what reaches eidolon from a request) says so in one sentence.
- 202: {rid, state: "running", chat} only when a chat was given, so the page can tell an older perch that dropped it. Without one, exactly {rid, state} (tests/runs.rs:664-666 stays green).

What the reads return:
- row() (state.rs:368-387) inserts "chat" only when run.chat passes id_ok, so a hand-edited runs.json cannot hand the page a path or markup. statefile::load checks no field (state.rs:257-261). Every answer built from row() then carries it: the list (state.rs:479-482), the detail (state.rs:390-401), cancel's and abandon's answers.
- busy() (state.rs:559-565): the 409 body gains "chat" (the holder's tag, when it passes id_ok), so the page can say which chat holds the one shared browser. The sentence is unchanged.

GET /hub/runs?chat=<id>:
- route() (state.rs:466-477) passes req.uri().query() to list(); verb() keeps reading method and path only (state.rs:437-463).
- A pure `fn chat_query(query: Option<&str>) -> Result<Option<&str>, &'static str>`, in the style of log.rs parse_query (runs/log.rs:54-71):
  - None or "": no filter.
  - Exactly one pair `chat=<raw>` whose raw value passes id_ok AS IS, with no percent-decoding ('%' fails id_ok): filter on it.
  - Anything else is a 400 via problem() with a sentence: `?chat=`, `?chat=a&chat=b`, `?x=1`, `?limit=5`, `?chat=a&x=1`, `?chat=a%2Fb`, `?chat=..`, `?chat=a=b`.
- The filter runs BEFORE take(LISTED), still newest first (state.rs:268-272, 480).
- No existence check on a read: an unknown or deleted chat lists [].
- Other verbs keep ignoring a query as today.

Docs, in the same commit:
- state.rs:4-17 (the route table and the row) and 35-37 (the eidolon note).
- runs/README.md:18-38 (routes) and 40-44 (refusals, the row), plus a short paragraph "The chat tag":
  - it is the page's claim, a label and never proof or authority;
  - checked when written and when read;
  - it never reaches eidolon;
  - pruning at KEPT is across all chats (state.rs:326-330);
  - a perch from before RT reads a tagged runs.json but its next write drops every tag (write() rewrites the whole file, state.rs:249-253).
live_check:
Fake perch on PORT=48142 with this slice's own perch and fake_eidolon (a perch slice: private target per WAVE3.md), FAKE_PERCH_BASE=$HOME/.cache/RT-live, FAKE_PERCH_ARGS="--run-graphs wiki-hop --plugins-dir /mnt/c/Users/dxcen/Projects/Minerva/eidolon-plugins" and FAKE_PERCH_ENV="FAKE_WORKFLOW_CASE=$HOME/.cache/RT-live/case FAKE_WORKFLOW_STEP_MS=300" (the case file holds `a`). Health flags are left off, so a start waits for no service (runs/README.md:104-105). All via curl with the bearer from a 0600 header file (the fake-perch.sh pattern):
1. Copy perch/tests/fixtures/jev/a/journal.ndjson to <T>/minerva/sessions/1700000000001.eid (the fake perch's sessions dir, fake-perch.sh:130), then GET /hub/sessions: it lists 1700000000001.
2. POST /hub/runs {graph:wiki-hop, args:{start:Ancient_Egypt}, chat:1700000000001}: 202 with chat. GET /hub/runs/r1, GET /hub/runs and GET /hub/runs?chat=1700000000001 each carry it.
3. POST with chat c0ffee99: 404 {error:no such chat}. With chat ../x: 400. `ls <T>/minerva/runs` gains nothing.
4. POST with no chat: 202 {rid:r2, state} with no chat key. GET /hub/runs?chat=1700000000001 is [r1] only. ?chat=a&chat=b and ?chat=a%2Fb: 400.
5. grep -r 1700000000001 <T>/minerva/runs/: no hit (argv, config.toml, args.json, logs). stat runs.json: 0600.
6. Write `b` to the case file, start beside the chat (parks), then start again: the 409 body names run r3 and chat 1700000000001.
7. No restart by hand. Do not stop the perch, edit runs.json and start it again: fake-perch.sh --stop removes the whole tree (fake-perch.sh:91-92), a start refuses a tree that exists (fake-perch.sh:98), and a perch launched outside the script loses its env -i, temp HOME and XDG isolation (fake-perch.sh:146-153), so it would read the operator's eidolon config and sessions (config.rs:47-76) against BRIEF.md's isolation rule. A tag edited into runs.json by hand is covered by tests/runs.rs a_chat_written_into_runs_json_by_hand_is_left_off_the_row.
8. --stop. Then list the browser-pane steps for the orchestrator: none, the page change is GP-a.
risk: The tag is the page's claim, not where a run came from: nothing may grant authority because of it. If an agent route for runs is ever added, it must filter by agent::Caller.chat (agent/mod.rs:53-60), never by a body or query value. A chat id becomes a filter key and a stored string, never a path, argv word, env value or config key. An older perch silently drops tags on its next write (said in the README). The existence check reads directories under spawn_blocking on every tagged start; known_cwd answers first from memory for a chat the perch holds or remembers.
notes: Decisions taken for the readers' unknowns (perch-runs map), none of them reopen the user's design:

U1 which chats are known: term's rule exactly (known_cwd or list), so a chat in the trash whose folder is still remembered can be tagged, as it can open a terminal. One shared Registry::knows for term and runs is a follow-up for the sessions/term owners.

U2 holder: option A. The page keeps its unfiltered list poll, which it already needs for the no-chat view (GP-a); the perch's 409 stays the authority and now names the holder's chat. /hub/runs/health is not changed, and ?chat= means only that chat's runs.
U3 live-elsewhere roster chats and eidolon's own read-only chats (origin other) can be tagged: list() includes both (sessions.rs:793-827), and the tag is only a label.
U4 forks: a fork is a new id (fork.rs:37) and does not inherit its source's runs. U5 there is no re-tag route. U7 id reuse is accepted: ids are millisecond stamps.

Out of scope, seen in passing: journal_of and answer trust the `session` path from runs.json (state.rs:415-418, 597) without proc.rs decide's inside-the-run-folder check (proc.rs:495-501), and term's Record::vetted filters chat with screen::shown, which is weaker than id_ok (term/mod.rs:201). Follow-ups for their owners, not this slice.
